issues.claim: Partly fixed (round-0 id kept; same defect as peer VM-R2T-06). R2-25 (a) rules '§2.6's water table (VEW-04's text, with its EP-22 fixture)'. §2.6 now reads a moat's one derived level (base l.1901–1902), but the fixture was not written: the model seat handed it to pipeline (repair-r2-model HAND-OFFS) and §4.13's EP-22 row (l.8808) still names only 'a hill town with moat: all, an arid town with no river with moat: inner' and the dry-ditch rung. No other bar tests a plot beside a wet moat (T-V4-80 (j) tests sewer outfalls only), so the moat × slope edge, whose old outcome was a silent wrong cellar rung, has its outcome but no test.
issues.required_change: §4.13, EP-22's case cell: the hill-town fixture adds 'a plot within `waterTableM` of a wet moat on the slope reads the moat's derived level (§4.2 S3 (10)) + `freeboardCm` as its water table, never its bank top — its cellar or crypt taking the full rung where that level allows (§2.6)'; its outcome cell adds '§2.6's water table'.

issues.claim: A raised way laid BEFORE an enceinte trace that later crosses it (walls × raised ways; opened by round 2's crossing station; not in the catalogue; distinct from peer VM-R2T-03, the band's decay under a station). §2.7's crossing station (support step (3), base l.2528–2536) is laid only when the support step runs — 'after its course and deck level are fixed and before the span rule' (l.2512–2513) — and no text re-runs it when a trace or moat is later laid across a standing raised way. At generation: a viaduct is raised 'inside S4's route solve (and each later stage's S5b through this router)' (§4.3 The slot, l.5590–5591), before every later stage's trace; S5b makes the existing arterials' crossings of the new boundary its gates (l.5769–5776), so a stage-k+1 gate falls on the deck; S5a's Outer moats (l.5754–5765) carve the channel, put a fresh part-0 deck on 'the arterial just outside each gate' and state 'Nothing finer than L1 exists yet, so the carve's footprint clears nothing' although the viaduct's pier footprints stand on ground part 0; §4.8 S7 lays no raised gate (only V06's epoch rule names one). At an epoch: V06 §3.7.6 (5) crosses a standing aqueduct or viaduct 'only under a span over land, never through a support' (V06 l.1570–1571), i.e. between stations, while J-V6.140 and the same item call the opening 'the deck's station on the trace … its pier the wall's band' (l.1582–1583, l.4385); V06 §3.7.1 widens t_k until every existing footprint is at least the strip's width + growth.ringBlockM from the boundary (l.1435–1437) and §3.7.6 (5) counts the raised way's supports as footprints, which at the masonry pitch of 8–15 m (V11 l.3942) against an 18–33 m strip (§4.8 l.7469–7472) no boundary across the raised way can satisfy. As written the earlier stations stand: piers left in the new ring's setback, glacis, berm and moat channel (the carve clears nothing; §5.3 has no invariant on a support in water), no station on the trace, the clear-span bound never re-read — a silent wrong result against §2.7's 'no support in water' and T110-2's '0 piers in a setback, glacis, berm or moat'; at an epoch an unsatisfiable widening (T-V6-47 expects the crossing under a span). T110-2's crossing fixtures (l.17988–17992) cover only a course laid after the wall it crosses.
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step: add '(6) A trace or moat laid across a standing raised way — a later stage's S5a trace and outer moat at generation, an epoch's circuit, contraction or re-anchored stretch (V06 §3.7.6 (5)), a hand drawWall — re-runs (1)–(5) on that raised way in the same commit: the crossing station on the new trace (the nearest interior station within p ÷ 2 moved there, keeping its key, else one added), the stations in the new strip's setback, glacis, berm or channel slid or omitted by (3); where a clear span on either side of the station would then pass maxClearSpanM, or a pier maxPierM, the trace gives way (S5a: its stage trace takes the next lattice boundary node off that span, reported; V06: retrace and wait, walls.waited) — a standing raised way is never dropped for a wall.' Other ends this round (R2-05): §4.4 S5a Outer moats (pipeline) — 'the carve clears no raised-way support: (6) re-sites one first in the same commit; a stage gate on a raised arterial is a raised gate whose tower carries the deck, the deck itself crossing the channel (no part-0 deck added for it), the part-0 way beneath taking its own ground gate'; §4.8 S7 (pipeline) — the raised gate and the aqueduct's wall opening as generation furniture in V06 §3.7.6 (5)'s form; V06 §3.7.1 (V06) — its footprint-distance test excepts the supports of a raised way the trace crosses, within one strip width of the crossing; §13.2 T110-2 (scope) — a CITY c14 fixture whose S4 viaduct over a valley is crossed at a gate by stage 2's moated ring, and an epoch circuit across a standing aqueduct: each crossing's one station on the trace, 0 piers in a setback, glacis, berm or moat, the raised way kept.

issues.claim: Item 116's export bar at the METROPOLIS cap has two outcomes. §13.2's T116-4 (base l.18077–18078) now reads 'every export frames within the limit, the whole bounds at most, or stop 0's extent where the bounds are wider than the window at stop 0'. R2-30's clause describes a view; an export has no window (§11.2's export runs in the worker and in Node with no viewport), and §8.7, the export frame's home (l.13879–13882), cuts every export only to the limit bounds ('the whole limit bounds at most … a requested frame reaching past them is cut to them'), window-free, as item 116 (c) says ('EXPORTS frame within the same limit (the whole bounds at most)'). At the cap the bar either fails §8.7's whole-map export (a print of the 17.53 km frame cut to a window's stop-0 extent) or cannot be evaluated headless.
issues.required_change: T116-4 reads: 'every export frames within the limit bounds (§8.7: the whole bounds — town and camps while a crisis look stands — at most), at any window size and with none; at the METROPOLIS cap a whole-bounds PNG, print and SVG export frames the whole bounds'. R2-30's 'or stop 0 where the bounds are wider than the window at stop 0' stays in T116-1's view bar only.

issues.claim: Two crisis places have no reference line at a town no road reaches. §10.2 Crisis looks (d) defines the main approach road as 'the arterial out of the gate of greatest trade weight …, else the way of greatest trade weight leaving the built edge' (base l.15373–15375) and builds two places on it: approachByGate, the refugee camp ('the campLand faces along the main approach road by its gate, nearest V06's frontierFor', l.15381–15382), and outside, the quarantine camp ('the campLand faces furthest from the main approach road', l.15383). S3 (9) (a)'s mesa 'has no road in at generation and says so' (l.5381–5391), so no way leaves its built edge. Only approachRoads has a fallback there ('a place no road reaches (S3 (9) (a)'s unserved mesa) takes the campLand nearest its boundary'); V01 §3.18 defines campLand with no approach road and V07 §5.6 (7) the village rungs ('no entry — every camp on the campLand nearest the perimeter'), but at TOWN and above the refugee and quarantine camps have no line to rank by, and V06's frontierFor has no answer either (its no-frontier case is 'the approach road by a gate', R2-37 (6)). EP-27 names this mesa only for a siege; T-ER-27 has no such fixture.
issues.required_change: §10.2 (d): 'With no main approach road (no way leaves the built edge — S3 (9) (a)'s unserved mesa), approachByGate takes the campLand faces nearest frontierFor's answer, else nearest the boundary point closest to the centre, and outside the campLand faces furthest from that point'. V06 §3.22 (2) (V06's end): frontierFor's no-frontier answer is then that boundary point. EP-27 and T-ER-27 add the unserved mesa with a refugee camp and a quarantine standing: each on campLand, else on the ring marks, never undefined.

issues.claim: The per-bank field outfall can lie in, and run along, the water its bank's admission refused. V04 §3.2 N2 (V04 l.985–991) takes 'the D8 path of the cell of largest accumulation … among its stretch's cells not on water', follows it 'outward to its first cell outside R and beyond the outermost enceinte's outer strip', and lets 'its outfall run follow that D8 path back to the stretch's cell'. A cell 'not on water' still has its steepest-descent neighbour where the terrain sends it, and on a river bank that is the river: water faces lie outside R, so the path runs down the river bed until it passes the walls. For a river town whose candidates on one bank all lie upstream of a mill intake or harbour mouth (N2's outfall.below), with no moat, that bank's field outfall is { into: 'field', water: null } at a river cell and its outfall run lies over the water face — against N3's 'no edge lies over water' (J-V4.129), UC19 (V04 l.2444: 'no sewer edge, run … lies over a water face') and T-V4-80 (j)'s '0 sewer edges … over a water face'. The construction gives no fallback for it.
issues.required_change: V04 §3.2 N2's field outfall: 'the D8 path is followed over land only: the field outfall is the first cell of the path outside R and beyond the outermost enceinte's outer strip reached without entering a water face; a stretch cell whose path enters a water face first is passed over for the next by accumulation (ties by address); where every stretch cell's path does, the bank drains by gutter and pit, its area reported unsewered (F-NET's truncate rung)'. UC19 cites it. T-V4-80 (j) adds a river-town fixture whose bank's river candidates all lie upstream of a mill intake, moat: 'none': the field outfall on land beyond the strip and 0 outfall-run edges over a water face, or the bank unsewered and reported.

issues.claim: A siege's places read 'the outermost (standing) enceinte' — beyondWalls (base l.15376), outside (l.15383), edge (l.15388) and 'a siege of a place with no standing enceinte draws the blockade row' (l.15408) — undefined or wrong wherever a place's enceintes are not one nested series. Enceinte.kind includes bailey (§2.7 l.2236; Castle.curtain), so an unwalled town with a castle has a standing enceinte: its siege draws the trench and earthwork line 'round the walled arcs at the standoff', about 300 m round the castle, across the town's own plots and buildings, against the owner's 'an unwalled place gets blockade camps on its approach roads' (item 122 (b)). Rings that are not nested have no one outermost ring: a castle outside the town wall, a twin town's two rings (F-SITE's 'walls apart by the floor', l.8965), an aroundStage ring (§2.7 l.2242). And the siege line is kept off 'water, a way's carriageway, a gate's passage or a label's keep-out' only ((d), l.15370–15371), so it is drawn across extramural ribbon plots and buildings within the standoff of an ordinary walled town.
issues.required_change: §10.2 (d): 'The walls a siege reads are the place's enceintes of kinds other than bailey (a castle's curtain only along its shared stretch with the town wall, Castle.cityWeld; its keep is gatesAndKeep's); outermost is the outer envelope of their walled arcs — for rings that are not nested, the walled arcs of each ring that no other ring encloses'; 'a place with no standing enceinte' reads 'no standing town enceinte', so an unwalled town with a castle draws the blockade on its approach roads; and the siege line and every camp are never drawn on a building footprint (burned farmsteads draw on their own), the line broken where it would cross an extramural plot's building. EP-27 and T-ER-27 add: an unwalled TOWN with an inside castle, a walled CITY with an outside castle, a twin town with two rings, and a walled town with extramural ribbons inside the standoff — 0 look pixels on a building footprint and the blockade at the castle-only town.
